title: Mara and the Wreck
premise: Mirabel Voss, a desert ranger with a stolen compass and a debt she can't name aloud, is hired to track a thief who vanished upriver into the drowned country beyond the salt flats. When the expedition's radio goes silent, she finds the camp gutted and its leader, Sef Adama, hiding a secret: the thief stole not money but a map to the Wreck, a pre-flood vessel rumored to hold the region's lost water rights. As monsoon season closes in, Mirabel and Sef must navigate leaking channels, rival claim-jumpers, and her own growing suspicion that the compass she carries was forged from the same charts. At the Wreck itself, Mirabel learns her family's debt was incurred buying those very rights—and that survival means deciding whether to sell them or drown them. In the end she burns the claims, keeps only the compass, and walks back into the desert owning nothing but her name.
about_author: P. M. Kavanagh is the pen name of a former river surveyor who spent six seasons mapping floodplains before turning to fiction. They write adventure stories about people whose debts are larger than their boats.

chapters.title: Salt and Silence
chapters.summary: Mirabel Voss tracks a thief across the salt flats, following boot prints that end at a river no map admits to. Her POV establishes her debt, her cracked compass, and her rule of staying invisible. The emotional beat: loneliness worn as armor.

chapters.title: The Hiring
chapters.summary: In the river town of Callow's Landing, an expedition chief named Sef Adama offers Mirabel double pay to find his missing surveyor—the thief. She takes it despite misgivings. POV: Mirabel. Beat: greed wrestling with instinct.

chapters.title: Upriver
chapters.summary: The expedition boat pushes into flooded forest; radio contact with the advance camp dies mid-sentence. POV: alternating Mirabel and deckhand Toma, who suspects sabotage. Beat: unease hardening into dread as the channel narrows.

chapters.title: What the Water Kept
chapters.summary: They find the advance camp looted, one survivor delirious, muttering about 'the Wreck' and 'the paper.' POV: Mirabel. Beat: first confrontation with the idea that the theft was about inheritance, not coin.

chapters.title: Leaking
chapters.summary: Monsoon squalls open seams in the hull; they beach on a drowned church steeple overnight. POV: Toma, revealing he once worked for the claim-broker Harrow. Beat: trust fraying—everyone aboard has a price.

chapters.title: The Stranger
chapters.summary: A lone poler, Ilsa Renn, rescues them from a collapsing channel and guides them through backwaters for a cut of whatever they find. POV: Mirabel. Beat: reluctant alliance; Ilsa reads the water like scripture.

chapters.title: Harrow's Men
chapters.summary: Claim-jumpers shadow them, flying broker colors; a night skirmish costs them fuel and Toma's silence breaks—he confesses he sold their route to Harrow. POV: Toma. Beat: betrayal, and the crew's choice to keep him anyway.

chapters.title: Charts in the Dark
chapters.summary: Sef shows Mirabel the stolen map fragment: the Wreck holds sealed water-rights deeds predating the flood. Mirabel recognizes the drafting style of her own grandfather. POV: Mirabel. Beat: the debt she carries suddenly has a shape.

chapters.title: Deadfall Channel
chapters.summary: Ilsa leads them through a snare-filled shortcut; a harpoon trap wounds Sef, and Mirabel must choose between speed and blood. POV: Ilsa, revealing she was paid by Harrow too—but has changed her mind. Beat: loyalty bought, not given.

chapters.title: The Drowned Town
chapters.summary: They shelter in a submerged village where Mirabel finds her family name carved on a deed-box lid. POV: Mirabel. Beat: inheritance stops being abstract—it has her face on it.

chapters.title: Radio Ghosts
chapters.summary: A working transmitter picks up Harrow's network: he knows where they're going and what Mirabel is. Sef confronts her; she lies badly. POV: Sef. Beat: the partnership cracks over secrets both are keeping.

chapters.title: Mutiny Weather
chapters.summary: Storm strands them mid-channel; rations fail; Toma argues for turning back, Ilsa for pressing on. A vote nearly comes to knives. POV: Toma. Beat: hunger stripping the crew to its true motives.

chapters.title: The Compass Test
chapters.summary: Mirabel admits her compass points not north but toward the Wreck—her grandfather built it from the same charts. Ilsa calls it a key, Sef a leash. POV: Mirabel. Beat: the tool of her invisibility becomes the mark of her lineage.

chapters.title: Ambush at the Fork
chapters.summary: Harrow's men trap them at the channel fork; the escape costs the boat's engine and Toma volunteers as decoy and doesn't come back. POV: Ilsa. Beat: grief and guilt; the price of survival gets a face.

chapters.title: Poling the Dead Water
chapters.summary: Engineless, they pole through stagnant backwater for three days, hallucinating, rationing breath as much as food. POV: Mirabel. Beat: endurance as devotion—what survives when everything else is spent.

chapters.title: The Wreck
chapters.summary: They reach it: a pre-flood barge fused into a hillside, its hold sealed, the deeds inside intact. Harrow waits on deck with Toma, alive, as leverage. POV: Mirabel. Beat: awe curdling into confrontation.

chapters.title: Bargain
chapters.summary: Harrow offers Mirabel her family's debt erased if she signs the rights to him; Sef urges burning them; Toma begs her to take the deal. POV: Toma. Beat: every character's philosophy laid bare at gunpoint.

chapters.title: High Water
chapters.summary: The monsoon crest hits; the Wreck begins to shift. In the chaos Mirabel seizes the deeds, Harrow falls to the flood, and Toma chooses to stay behind holding the line. POV: Mirabel. Beat: climax—survival demanded a payment she finally names.

chapters.title: Ash and Ink
chapters.summary: On high ground, Mirabel burns the deeds while Sef watches, furious then resigned; Ilsa keeps only the map fragment as a souvenir. POV: Sef. Beat: power refused, and the strange freedom of having nothing left to lose.

chapters.title: Settlement
chapters.summary: They drift downstream to Callow's Landing, where Harrow's syndicate collapses without the deeds and the water rights revert to common law. POV: Ilsa. Beat: the world slightly repaired, at personal cost.

chapters.title: What Mirabel Owes
chapters.summary: Mirabel settles her original debt honestly, coin by coin, refusing shortcuts. She tells the truth about her grandfather for the first time. POV: Mirabel. Beat: inheritance redefined as responsibility, not possession.

chapters.title: North, Sort Of
chapters.summary: Mirabel walks back into the desert, compass in hand, now pointing wherever she decides to go. Ilsa's silhouette follows at a distance. POV: Mirabel. Beat: resolution—invisibility chosen freely at last, and no longer alone.
